definition: In machine learning, a probabilistic classifier is a classifier that is able to predict, given an observation of an input, a probability distribution over a set of classes, rather than only outputting the most likely class that the observation should belong to.
details: Probabilistic classifiers provide classification that can be useful in its own right or when combining classifiers into ensembles.

explainer.lead: A probabilistic classifier outputs a probability distribution over classes instead of only the single most likely label. It matters because downstream decisions often need confidence, not just a guess.

tiers.eli5: Rather than saying 'this is a cat', it says '70% cat, 30% dog', so you know how sure it is.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use the full distribution to set thresholds, abstain on uncertain cases, and combine classifiers into ensembles. A pitfall is treating the probabilities as well-calibrated when they often are not.
tiers.paperLevel: Given an observation of an input, a probabilistic classifier predicts a probability distribution over a set of classes rather than only the most likely class; the output can be used directly or when combining classifiers into ensembles.

explainer.example: An email filter outputs 0.92 spam and 0.08 not-spam, letting the system route borderline messages to a human review queue.
